Copper -Catalyzed/T sOH-Pr omoted T andem Annulation of 1,6-
Allenynes with Organic Azides

Abstract: A copper -catalyzed/T sOH-promoted one-
pot tandem annulation of 1,6-allenynes with organic
azides was reported, providing N-allyl 1,2,3-
triazole-fused structures in moderate to excellent
yields under mild reaction conditions. Moreover , the
late-stage diversification of the N-allyl products can
be realized by chemoselectively reducing to the N-
alkyl counterparts.
Keywords: CuAAC; one-pot protocol; tandem reac-
tion; 1,2,3-triazole-fused structure
1,2,3-T riazole and its fused systems have gained
significant attention due to their broad applications in
medicinal chemistry
[1]
and materials science.
[2]
Among
them, fused 1,2,3-triazole and azine ring systems as a
useful class of hybrid heterocycles have interesting
pharmacological activities (Figure 1).
[3]
Developing
eff icient and versatile routes toward 1,2,3-triazoloazine
structures is therefore highly desirable.
[4]
N-sulfonyl-1,2,3-triazoles, which can be easily
prepared from copper-catalyz ed azide-alkyne cyclo-
additions (CuAAC),
[5]
have received much attention
because of their useful transformations through α-
imino metal carbenes
[6]
or N-sulfonly ketenimines
[7]
concomitant with denitrogenative ring opening. How-
ever , in comparison with its NH-1,2,3-triazole ano-
logues for the synthesis of N-substituted 1,2,3-
triazoles,
[8]
N-sulfonyl-1,2,3-triazoles have been rela-
tively less developed.
[9–12]
In 2016, Chen’ s group
reported an effi cient Brønsted acid-promoted N
2
-
selective addition of N-sulfonyl-1,2,3-triazoles to
olefins for the synthesis of N-alkyl-1,2,3-triazoles
(Scheme 1a, equiv . 1);
[9]
meanwhile, Shi’ s group devel-
oped a novel base-induced synthesis of N-
dialkylaminomethyl-1,2,3-triazoles through N
2
-selec-
tive addition of N-sulfonyl-1,2,3-triazoles to iminiums
(Scheme 1a, equiv . 2);
[10]
later , a gold-catalyzed N
2
-
selective addition of N-sulfonyl-1,2,3-triazoles to vinyl
ethers was developed by Zhao and coworkers (Sche-
me 1a, equiv . 3);
[1 1]
subsequently , the same group
further realized a gold-catalyzed N
1
-selective addition
of N-sulfonyl-1,2,3-triazoles to alkynes, providing N-
vinyl-1,2,3-trizoles (Scheme 1a, equiv . 4).
[12]
Despite
these intermolecular advances, little attention has been
paid to the intramolecular versions of N-sulfonyl-1,2,3-
triazoles for the synthesis of 1,2,3-triazole-fused
structures.
[13]
On the other hand, N-allenamides are versatile
building blocks and highly susceptible towards

tures.

Brønsted acid or metal promoted electrophilic
activation.
[14]
Thus, we envisioned that if the R group
of N-sulfonyl-1,2,3-triazoles is an allenamide, the
intramolecular N
3
-selective nucleophilic cyclization
might occur to provide N-allyl-1,2,3-triazole-fused
structures (Scheme 1b).
Based on the hypothesis and in continuation with
our interest in allene chemistry for developing novel
methodologies on polycyclic skeleton synthesis,
[15]
we
initially tried to synthesize the allenamide-tethered N-
sulfonyl-1,2,3-triazole 3 a via the CuAAC reaction of
1,6-allenyne 1 a with tosyl azide 2 a. Surprisingly , a
novel tricyclic 1,2,3-triazoloquinazoline 4 a was regio-
selectively obtained as single product after silica gel
chromatography (Scheme 1c). The structure of 4 a was
unambiguously confirmed by X-ray dif fraction
analysis.
[16]
Herein, we report our preliminary results.
The allenamide-tethered N-sulfonyl-1,2,3-triazoles
3 were prepared in situ via the well-developed CuT c-
catalyzed reaction of 1,6-allenyne 1 a with the corre-
sponding organic azides 2.
[5]
According to the previous
reports,
[9–12]
trace amount of water is auxiliary to
capture the leaving p-toluenesulfonyl (T s) group. W e
first conducted the reaction in toluene at room temper-
ature with SiO
2
as catalyst, water as addtive and
obtained the desired product 4 a in 68% yield (T able 1,
Entry 1). Control experiments without catalyst or with
4 Å molecular sevies (MS) as additve yielded no
product (Entries 2–3). Besides p-toluenesulfonyl (R =
T s) group, other sulfonyl groups were also tested,
while methanesulfonyl (R = Ms) group gave inferior
result (Entry 4) and p-nitrobenzenesulfonyl (R = Ns)
group afforded no product at all (Entry 5). Then,
diff erent solvents were screened. In general, aromatic
solvents were better than others for this one-pot
reaction (Entries 6–9). Both benzene and xylenes gave
comparable results, whereas other solvents such as
acetonitrile (MeCN) and tetrahydrofuran (THF) were
not suitable for the reaction. At the stage of substrate
investigation, however , we found that SiO
2
showed
poor catalytic performance for functionalized sub-
strates (T able 2). Thus, various acids were examined.
The reaction did not work with H
2
SO
4
as catalyst
(Entry 10). Gratifyingly , MsOH and T sOH gave prod-
uct 4 a in 55% and 69% yields respectively within
5 min (Entries 1 1–12). In addition, Lewis acid such as
AlCl
3
was also tested, aff ording only moderate result
(Entry 13). Though T sOH-promoted autocatalytic
transformation of N-tosyl-1,2,3-triazoles was
reported,
[17]
a decrease of the catalyst loading gave
product 4 a in 47% yield (Entry 14). A longer reaction
time led to no significant improvement (Entry 15),
while high temperature resulted no desired product
because the allenyne substrate is unstable at high
temperature (Entry 16).
[18]
W ith the optimal reaction conditions in hand, we
next set out to investigate the substrate scope. V arious
aniline-derived 1,6-allenynes were subjected to this
reaction (T able 2). First, the 1,6-allenyne substrates
with other sulfonyl groups than p-toluenesulfonyl
substituent all proceeded well to give the correspond-
ing products in moderate to excellent yields, except
that the methylsulfonyl substrate aff orded the desired
product 4 f in only 22% yield (4 a–f). Ester group (R =
CO
2
Me) instead was also suitable for the reaction and
the corresponding product 4 g was obtained in 41%
yield. Then, the reaction of tosyl azide 2 a with
diff erent substituted 1,6-allenynes bearing electron-
donating or electron-withdrawing substituents at the
random position of the aryl moiety all proceeded
smoothly to provide the desired products in moderate
to excellent yields (4 h–u). Furthermore, both di-
substituted 1,6-allenynes and the bulky naphthyl one
were all well tolerated for the reaction (4 v–y). When

standard reaction conditions, the corresponding allena-

tained in almost quantitative yield, which could trans-
form to 4 z in 41% yield at elevated temperature.
[18]
Gratifyingly , 1,6-allenyne 1a’ (R
2
= Me) furnished the
desired product 4a’ in 75% yield. It is worth noting
that T sOH showed better functional group compatibil-
ity than SiO
2
in most cases (4 j–k, 4 q, and 4 x). Gram-
scale synthesis was also performed under standard
reaction conditions and gave product 4 a in 65% yield.
Besides the 1,6-allenyne substrates bearing an
aromatic linker , benzo-free aliphatic 1,6-allenyne 1b’
was also investigated (Scheme 2a). Although the
allenamide-tethered N-sulfonyl-1,2,3-triazole 3b’ could
be isolated in 90% yield, no desired product but rather
complex mixture was obtained when 3b’ was subjected
to T sOH in toluene at room temperature.
[19]
This failure
indicates that the aromatic linker is essential for the
reaction and may stabilize the reaction intermediate.
Gratifyingly , phenoxyallene-based 1,6-allenyne 1c’
was suitable for this reaction (Scheme 2b). The
phenoxyallene-tethered N-sulfonyl-1,2,3-triazole 3c’
was isolated in 93% yield, further aff ording the desired
product 4c’ in only 25% yield maybe due to the
relatively poor electron-donating property of
oxygen.
[18]
T o further expand the reaction scope, we
turned our attention into other two types of allenyne
substrates bearing allenoate (Scheme 2c) and unbiased
allene (Scheme 2d). Unfortunately , the corresponding
desired products were not detected althouth the
relevant N-sulfonyl-1,2,3-triazoles were obtained.
On the basis of previous reports,
[9–12]
two plausible
catalytic cycles are depicted in Scheme 3. The allena-
mide-tethered N-sulfonyl-1,2,3-triazole 3 a is generated
in situ from 1 a and 2 a via CuAAC reaction. Then, an
iminium cation intermediate I is generated from the
allenamide with the addition of a proton,
[14]
which is
then attacked by the internal N
3
-nitrogen of the triazole
to give the intermediate II. Then, the activated S–N
bond is hydrolyzed to form the desired product 4 a
concomitant with the release of T sOH and a proton
(path a, Scheme 3). On the other hand, the T sOH-
catalyzed hydrolyzation of N-sulfonyl-1,2,3-triazole 3 a
is possible and aff ords NH-1,2,3-triazole III. Then, an
iminium cation intermediate IV is generated from the
allenamide with the addition of a proton, which is then
attacked by the internal N
3
-nitrogen of triazole to give

The versatility of this T sOH-promoted CuAAC
annulation can be further exploited in chemoselective
reduction (Scheme 4). The N-allyl-1,2,3-triazole prod-
ucts 4 could be readily reduced to the corresponding
N-alkyl counterparts via Pd/C-catalyzed chemoselec-
tive hydrogenation under H
2
in isopropyl alcohol (IP A)
at room temeprature.
In summary , we have developed a copper -cata-
lyzed/T sOH-promoted one-pot tandem annulation of
1,6-allenynes with orga nic azides to provide N-allyl
1,2,3-triazole-fused structures in moderate to excellent
yields under mild reaction conditions. Moreover , the
N-allyl-1,2,3-triazole products could be readily reduced
to the N-alkyl counterparts. Further studies will be
reported in due course.
Experimental Section
General Procedur e for the Prepar ation of Com-
pounds 4
T osyl azide 2 a (0.2 mmol, 1.0 equiv .) was added into a solution
of 1,6-allenynes 1 (0.2 mmol, 1.0 equiv .) and CuT c (10 mol%)
in toluene (2.0 mL). The mixture was stirred at room temper -
ature for 12 h. Then, H
2
O (0.2 mmol, 1.0 equiv .) and T sOH
(100 mol%) were successively added at room temperature.
After the reaction was completed (monitored by TLC), the
resulting mixture was quenched with saturated NaHCO
3
(aq)
and extracted with EtOAc. The combined organic phase was
concentrated under reduced pressure and the residue was
purified by flash chromatography (silica gel, hexanes/EtOAc/
DCM as eluent) to af ford the corresponding products 4.
